subject.title: fix(status): use legacy Codex OAuth profiles for OpenAI usage

question: Should OpenClaw provider-usage runtime accept retired `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles for canonical `openai` usage, or should affected users be required to run `openclaw doctor --fix` first?
rationale: Repository policy says legacy `openai-codex` state belongs in doctor/migration paths, while this PR deliberately adds a narrow live runtime compatibility exception for status usage.

options.title: Approve usage-only legacy bridge
options.body: Accept the runtime fallback for stored legacy OAuth/token profiles while keeping API keys excluded and rebasing onto the current provider-usage auth shape.

options.title: Keep doctor-only migration
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want status usage to work only after legacy profiles are migrated to canonical `openai:*` IDs.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Require a follow-up patch that documents the removal boundary and proves the fallback cannot overlap with Codex synthetic app-server usage.

recommendation.title: Approve usage-only legacy bridge
recommendation.body: Accept the runtime fallback for stored legacy OAuth/token profiles while keeping API keys excluded and rebasing onto the current provider-usage auth shape.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the compatibility boundary created by the OpenAI provider identity migration that steipete authored and merged.
